key_insight: Tree-based machine learning models can accurately predict halide-perovskite band gaps from atomic and structural descriptors, with B-site and X-site chemistry being the strongest drivers.
engineering_relevance: These models can speed up lead-free perovskite screening by guiding composition design toward target band gaps for optoelectronic and solar-cell applications.
method: Trained ensemble tree-based regressors on atomic and structural features.
Compared RFR, GBRT, and XGB for band-gap prediction.
Used feature-importance analysis to identify dominant descriptors.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong predictive accuracy across multiple halide-perovskite families and highlights consistent feature-importance patterns.
watch_item: Model performance may depend on the diversity and coverage of the training data, so extrapolation to unseen perovskite chemistries should be treated cautiously.
paper_title: Machine learning insights into band gap properties in halide-based perovskites
